reproduction_target: Corgi, a context-aware DNA sequence-to-function deep-learning model: curation of a 580-sample multi-assay human dataset (ENCODE, FANTOM5, Tabula Sapiens/CATlas, 10x multiome), trans-regulator gene-set definition, TPM harmonization (quantile normalization + pyComBat batch correction), leakage-controlled train/validation/test split on Borzoi folds, model training (~196M parameters, ~200 A100 GPU-days), benchmarking in cross-cell-type / cross-sequence / cross-both regimes, comparisons against EpiGePT (webserver), Borzoi (HuggingFace ensemble) and Avocado (retrained), Captum/DeepLift contribution scores with tangermeme seqlet-to-motif matching (HOCOMOCO v13 Core), and GSEApy/enrichr enrichment. No wet-lab component.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the Methods sections 'Data sources', 'Defining trans-regulatory factors', 'Training-test split', 'Data preprocessing', 'Model architecture', 'Model training', 'Benchmarking' and 'Contribution score calculation'. The four 10x-multiome preprocessing tools (scanpy, celltypist, multiVI, sinto, deepTools) are folded into one pseudobulk-bigwig step. Two public repositories are declared: https://github.com/ekinda/corgi (model, data processing, training scripts) and https://github.com/ekinda/corgi-reproduction (figure notebooks fig2-fig7). Stage-1 read of the corgi-reproduction README shows a venv + requirements-reproduction.txt install path plus a separate fully '==' pinned environment.txt dump; whether that dump actually resolves and covers the executed steps is a stage-2 question, so version stays <= 1 everywhere here.

steps.label: ENCODE sample selection: database scan for human samples with RNA-seq plus CAGE/RAMPAGE, or DNase-seq + >=1 histone ChIP-seq, or >=4 experiments on replicates of the same sample; error-tagged data and 6 low-FRiP CTCF samples excluded; 373 samples (Supplementary Table 5)
FANTOM5 CAGE-seq enrichment: manual curation matching 65 FANTOM5 CAGE experiments to selected ENCODE samples plus 119 new FANTOM5 samples (Supplementary Table 6)

Single-cell expansion: 71 pseudobulked Tabula Sapiens scRNA-seq samples matched to CATlas snATAC-seq bigwigs (descartes.brotmanbaty.org); matched expression from Fu et al. via s3://2023-get-xf2217/get_demo
10x multiome (brain, PBMC) preprocessing from h5ad/BAM into per-pseudobulk bigwig coverage using scanpy, celltypist, multiVI, sinto and deepTools; 17 pseudobulk samples added

trans-regulator gene-set definition: 1892 Aerts Lab TFs (hg38) + 324 literature-curated co-activators + 167 dbEM chromatin modifiers + 741 RBPWorld RBPs, de-duplicated and filtered to the ENCODE RNA-seq pipeline gene set = 2891 genes (Supplementary Table 2)

Expression harmonization: log-transform of coding-gene TPMs, quantile normalization to the total-RNA-seq reference distribution, batch correction across the 4 assay types with pyComBat; reference distribution shipped for user re-use

Training/validation/test split: agglomerative clustering of 580 samples into 40 expression clusters, whole-cluster hold-out, keyword-matched removal of similar cell types, random 'easy-test' draw; sequence folds from Borzoi (fold 3 test, fold 4 validation) with trans-regulator gene bodies excluded; 11,496 / 1462 / 1437 sequences of 524,288 bp

Output signal preprocessing: bigwig coverage scaled and soft-clipped with assay-specific parameters 'similar to the processing pipeline of Borzoi', then aggregated to 64 bp bins (sum for CAGE/RAMPAGE, sqrt of sum for RNA-seq, mean otherwise)

Corgi model architecture: 9 transformer layers, multi-head attention at 64 bp resolution with FiLM conditioning, FlashAttention v2, grouped-query attention (4 groups, 8 heads, 192 dims), rotary encodings on first 128 dims, ~196M trainable parameters, 22 output channels over the central 393 kb

Corgi training: adapted Poisson-multinomial loss with learnable per-channel weights, 5 epochs on NVIDIA A100 (~200 GPU-days), batch size 2, AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0.01 (MLP) / 0.001 (rest), bfloat16 mixed precision, cosine annealing with 3000 warmup steps, dynamic augmentation (Borzoi custom hg38 with gnomAD SNPs edited in at p=0.5, +/-3 bp shift, random reverse complement); no hyperparameter tuning

Benchmarking / correlation evaluation: 637 test-fold regions of 524 kb tiled at 393 kb stride (cross-sequence, cross-both) and 947 random training-fold regions (cross-cell type); 8192 bins cropped to central 6144; Pearson/Spearman on ~3.9M concatenated values in the squashed scale; test-time augmentation by shift + reverse-complement averaging

EpiGePT comparison: authors state 'We were unable to run the provided code to train our own version of EpiGePT' and used the online webserver https://health.tsinghua.edu.cn/epigept/ on 5 cell types (#124, #192, #213, #277, #323), 163,304 bins of 128 bp from chr8, Corgi average-pooled 64 bp -> 128 bp

Borzoi comparison (cross-sequence): 30 training samples matched to Borzoi tracks (Supplementary Table 4), same sequence folds with fold 3 as test, Borzoi 4-model ensemble from https://huggingface.co/johahi/borzoi-replicate-0 (0 through 3), mean of replicates, 32 bp -> 64 bp average pooling

Avocado imputation comparison: Avocado trained on the ENCODE subset of the Corgi training folds with test-cell-type RNA-seq bigwigs added; CAGE and ATAC samples excluded; validation every 100 epochs, best model at 2900 epochs; compared also against a training-mean baseline

Contribution scores: Captum DeepLift cis-contributions w.r.t. summed total-RNA-seq tracks with dinucleotide-shuffled baselines averaged over 20 shuffles; trans-contributions with mean expression across contexts as baseline
Seqlet identification and motif annotation with tangermeme (recursive_seqlets, annotate_seqlets) against HOCOMOCO v13 Core
Gene-set enrichment of top-contributing trans-regulators using the enrichr implementation from GSEApy

headline.static_readiness: 0/17 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 8/17 steps reach the stage-1 ceiling RI: model architecture, training, harmonization, signal preprocessing, benchmarking, Borzoi comparison, contribution scores and seqlet/motif analysis are all covered by the two declared public repositories plus a fully '==' pinned environment.txt in corgi-reproduction. The remaining 9 steps cap at NI for reasons that stage-2 cannot lift: manual curation of ENCODE/FANTOM5 sample sets and the trans-regulator gene list, unversioned single-cell preprocessing, the EpiGePT comparison run through a webserver after the authors state they could not run the published EpiGePT code, the Avocado retraining, and the enrichr call whose gene-set library and cutoffs are unstated. Realistic stage-2 upside is confined to the 8 RI steps.
headline.coverage: 17 computational steps assessed from Methods prose; no wet-lab steps (pure-computational paper). Code availability names two live repositories (github.com/ekinda/corgi, github.com/ekinda/corgi-reproduction); data availability names ENCODE/FANTOM5 (Supplementary Tables 5-6), CATlas bigwigs, Tabula Sapiens via an s3 path, and two 10x Genomics public datasets. Model checkpoints are on Zenodo record 18630048; the corgi-reproduction README's Zenodo link for reproduction_data.tar.gz is a 'to be updated' placeholder.

gaps.where: Software environment for the training pipeline (github.com/ekinda/corgi) vs the figure pipeline (github.com/ekinda/corgi-reproduction)
gaps.missing: The Methods prose pins only FlashAttention v2 and HOCOMOCO v13 Core. The corgi package README declares floating lower bounds (python>=3.9, torch>=2.1, flash-attn>=2.0.0, numpy>=1.24, pandas>=1.5, pyfaidx>=0.7, pybigwig>=0.3.22) with no lockfile or container. The corgi-reproduction repo ships a fully '==' pinned environment.txt (e.g. borzoi-pytorch==0.4.0, captum==0.8.0, celltypist==1.6.3, combat==0.3.3), but the README install path uses the unpinned requirements-reproduction.txt, so the lock is present-but-not-wired. No container digest, no conda-lock, no platform/CUDA pin.
gaps.how_to_close: Wire the pinned environment.txt (or a conda-lock/pixi.lock) into the documented install path, pin the training-side environment the same way, and publish a container digest that includes the CUDA/FlashAttention stack the A100 run depended on.

gaps.missing: The README states the archive must be downloaded from Zenodo, but the Zenodo URL is an empty placeholder annotated '(to be updated)'. Without it the declared figure notebooks have no inputs.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the reproduction data archive and replace the placeholder with the resolved Zenodo DOI/record URL.

gaps.where: C1, C2, C5, C7 - dataset curation and split construction
gaps.missing: Sample selection ('we scanned the ENCODE database', 'manually curated a list of samples'), the trans-regulator gene-list assembly from four literature/database sources, and the keyword-matched removal of similar cell types are described only as prose procedures with results deposited as supplementary tables. No script reconstructs the 580-sample set or the 40-cluster split from the raw sources.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship the curation and split scripts (ENCODE query, FRiP filter, agglomerative clustering call with its linkage/metric, keyword list) so the supplementary tables are regenerable rather than only readable.

gaps.missing: Unstated parameters: scanpy/celltypist/multiVI clustering and annotation settings; agglomerative clustering linkage and distance metric; the 'assay-specific' scaling and soft-clipping constants (only 'similar to Borzoi'); the dinucleotide-shuffle random seed; tangermeme recursive_seqlets thresholds and annotate_seqlets matching cutoffs; the enrichr gene-set library, background and significance cutoff.
gaps.how_to_close: Tabulate the assay-specific scaling/clipping constants, state clustering linkage/metric, expose seeds, and record the seqlet and enrichment thresholds in the config shipped with the code.

gaps.where: C10 Corgi training, C14 Avocado training
gaps.missing: No random seed is stated for Corgi training or for its stochastic augmentations (gnomAD allele edit-in at p=0.5, +/-3 bp shift, random reverse complement), nor for Avocado. Training cost is ~200 A100 GPU-days, so bit-level re-execution is out of reach for most re-users; released checkpoints (Zenodo 18630048) are the practical reproduction path.
gaps.how_to_close: Record seeds and the exact checkpoint-to-figure mapping, and state explicitly which figures are reproducible from released checkpoints without retraining.

gaps.missing: The comparison depends on a third-party webserver (https://health.tsinghua.edu.cn/epigept/) after the authors report they could not run the published EpiGePT training code. The served model version is not pinned and the server may change or disappear.
gaps.how_to_close: Archive the EpiGePT prediction outputs actually used (per-bin values for the 5 cell types on chr8) alongside the server access date and any reported model version.

gaps.where: C13 Borzoi ensemble, C3 Tabula Sapiens input
gaps.missing: External artifacts are named without immutable revisions: the HuggingFace repo johahi/borzoi-replicate-0..3 is cited without a commit SHA/revision, and the matched Tabula Sapiens expression is cited as an s3 path (s3://2023-get-xf2217/get_demo) with no versioning or access terms.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin HuggingFace revisions by SHA and mirror or checksum the s3-hosted expression matrices.

gaps.missing: Neither repository is cited at a release tag, commit SHA or archival DOI in the paper; only bare GitHub URLs are given, so the assessed state is a moving HEAD.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a paper release in both repos and archive them to Zenodo/Software Heritage, citing the DOI in the Code availability statement.
